newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU parliament draft attacks commission, UK on BSE.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament draft attacks commission, UK on BSE.

text.p: A draft European Parliament report on Monday strongly attacked Britain and the European Commission for mishandling the mad cow crisis but stopped short of demanding specific sanctions.
The report follows a four-months investigation by a special 19-member cross-party committee of inquiry into the epidemic, which has ravaged British herds and scared shoppers across the continent.

The 26-page Spanish-language draft, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, criticised the EU's executive Commission for delaying the release of data on the Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE) disease, saying this helped to undermine public confidence and worsen the economic damage.
The report, drafted by Spanish Socialist Manuel Medina, also attacked the British government's handling of the crisis, identifying 13 points of alleged negligence.
A parliamentary official said the report will be discussed by the inquiry committee at the Parliament's next plenary session starting in Strasbourg, France, on Monday.
"It could be amended," the official said, adding that European Commission President Jacques Santer is due to due to appear before the committee next week.
Neither Medina nor other members of the inquiry committee could be immediately be reached for comment. The Parliament is still in recess for the Christmas holidays.

The draft report accused London of failing to properly enforce a ban on animal feed exports containing meat and bone meal, pressing the European Commission to avoid inspecting British slaughterhouses between 1990-94 and failing to take adequate heed of scientific warnings.
EU officials said the criticisms were nothing new.
But they noted that the draft report took up an idea floated by EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler last month to create an independent agency to protect public and animal health.
The agency would help reinforce controls to ensure that export bans and other measures to combat mad cow disease were properly implemented.
The report called for speedier and wider publishing of data on BSE and to improve scientific advisory committees by making them more professional and politically independent.
The report, which is due to be adopted by the committee of inquiry on February 6, will then be submitted for approval by the European Parliament at a plenary session of February 17-21.
